sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Ganesh Green Bharat is an execution-led solar module, solar pump and EPC business pursuing a much larger battery-storage EPC opportunity. Its decisive strength is real manufacturing scale: audited operations revenue reached ₹1,064.27 crore in FY26, versus ₹318.01 crore in FY25. Its decisive weakness is conversion of accounting profits into freely available cash. Even on the favorable later FY24 comparative, FY24–26 cumulative CFO/PAT is only 13.40%. Subtracting investing-classified noncurrent-asset and deposit outflows makes that measure negative.

At the official 19 October 2026 close of ₹221.20, the headline historical P/E is low. That is not sufficient evidence of an investable bargain. G2 financial-reliability and G3 funding holds prevent a favorable classification. BQS, GQS (Growth Quality) and IAS remain NS, with exact missing-factor bounds rather than invented point scores. This is a growth/execution research watch, not an evidence-backed compounder. A certified opening liquidity/facility bridge, corrected comparative reporting, clean customer/supplier/deposit mapping and demonstrated project-level incremental returns would change the conclusion. Lower price alone would not resolve those holds. The separate rescue scenarios are hypothetical financing diagnostics, not expected returns or purchase recommendations.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The issuer is Ganesh Green Bharat Limited, formerly Ganesh Electricals Private Limited, CIN L31900GJ2019PLC108417, NSE Emerge symbol GGBL, ISIN INE0R8C01018. It listed on 12 July 2024. The research cutoff is 20 October 2026 in India; documents retrieved on 21 October are used only where their reported information predates the cutoff. The official 19 October NSE SM close is ₹221.20, with 24,801,000 issued shares and market capitalization of ₹548.59812 crore. These are dated references, not live executable prices.

Financials use consolidated Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not an assumed Ind AS framework. Souraj Energy is 74%-owned and the PIGL-GEPL joint venture is 50%. Parent-attributable PAT is used for equity earnings; group PAT matches group CFO. The investment horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, with a 15% nominal annual equity hurdle before personal taxes. A separate illustrative 12–16% nominal cost-of-capital range is not equated with that equity hurdle. ₹5 lakh is an illustrative execution reference, not a recommended allocation.

G1 is Conditional; G2 and G3 are Hold — unresolved; G4 is Conditional. Identity and exchange quote confidence are High. Historical transcription is Medium, but comparability, available current funding and incremental-return confidence are Low. Overall confidence is Low because material missing inputs prevent an investment conclusion. There is no supported finding of lending default, insolvency or fraud.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The canonical factor scores are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 6, R NS, D 4, P NS and L 6. Each factor audit records supporting facts, contrary evidence, confidence and source references.

BQS has a known weighted contribution of 4.34 and 88% coverage. Its mathematical missing-factor bounds are 4.46–5.54; its final score remains NS. GQS has a known contribution of 5.60 and 85% coverage, with raw bounds of 5.75–7.10. Persistent CASH 3 triggers a cap of 5 if the aggregate becomes complete, but does not replace its present NS status. IAS has a known contribution of 1.40 and 30% coverage, with raw bounds of 2.10–8.40. Q cannot be replaced with a BQS midpoint and R cannot be borrowed from the hypothetical rescue model.

The original framework weights and exact Decimal arithmetic are retained. Only complete aggregates would be rounded half-up to one decimal. Bounds are mathematical missing-data bounds, not confidence intervals, probabilities or ranks. Moving MOAT and DUR jointly by one point changes the BQS known contribution by 0.30 and GQS by 0.20; CAP remains missing. No governance-at-or-below-3 or evidenced funding-failure override is applied. All three aggregates remain outside numeric rankings.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The business manufactures solar PV modules and undertakes solar pumping, lighting, electrical and water-related EPC work. FY26 consolidated operations revenue comprises products of ₹930.0229 crore, services of ₹132.8355 crore and other operating revenue of ₹1.4099 crore. It is not a utility annuity: goods and project milestones require procurement, inspection, delivery and collection.

Management says more than 95% of materials are imported and describes roughly 75 days of inventory preparation, including 50–60 MW finished-product batches awaiting inspection before LC-backed dispatch. These are management explanations, not independent proof that every advance is recoverable. FY26 finished goods are ₹101.2036 crore and supplier advances ₹46.9996 crore. Government balances of ₹35.9401 crore also sit in short advances, so the entire ₹83.2819 crore balance is not supplier prepayment. Security/project deposits of ₹53.5482 crore add capital intensity beyond headline receivable days.

The emerging BESS opportunity involves procurement and EPC implementation, not automatic ownership of every storage asset described in the tender. The model therefore separates BESS execution from modules and legacy services; it does not add total contract value or operating property separately to enterprise value. Consolidation and non-controlling interests are retained consistently. Customer-level profitability, supplier concentration and a verified collection bridge remain important limitations, not evidence of impropriety by themselves.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
PSU qualification, functioning module lines, repeat installations and specification-compliant delivery are useful capabilities. They do not yet demonstrate structural pricing power. Management says standard price-escalation protection is absent, leaving contracted margins exposed to imported cells, glass, metals and foreign exchange. CARE highlights competition and technological obsolescence. Industry capacity expansion can compress returns even while installation demand grows.

Three primary-source economic comparators frame this risk. Solex reported FY26 revenue of ₹1,621.13 crore and an 11.52% operating margin with 4 GW of module capacity; its cell expansion and financing differ. Premier reported ₹7,824 crore of FY26 operating income and a 30.4% margin with integrated cells/modules. That integration and product mix make its margin unsuitable for direct transplantation to GGBL. Insolation Green, an operating subsidiary rather than the listed parent, reported FY25 total operating income of ₹1,269.56 crore and PBILDT of ₹160.12 crore, with major cell investment planned. Scope and rating-date differences are retained; no matched-date peer P/E ranking is fabricated.

GGBL can compete through reliable execution and procurement, but commodity inputs, smaller scale and tender economics constrain the moat score to 4. The decisive test is repeated margin and cash resilience across changing input prices and technology cycles, not customer logos or the size of the solar market.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Observed FY22–FY26 audited/restated operations revenues are ₹105.5367, ₹90.1991, ₹170.1702, ₹318.0119 and ₹1,064.2683 crore. Five observations contain four growth intervals, not five. Comparable FY21 revenue was not obtained, so the five-year CAGR is unavailable. The preselected three-year fallback, FY23–FY26, produces reported CAGR of 127.66%; the four-year FY22–FY26 CAGR is 78.20%. Annual revenue additions in FY23–FY26 are minus ₹15.3376 crore, then ₹79.9711 crore, ₹147.8417 crore and ₹746.2564 crore.

Souraj became a subsidiary from 1 April 2023, creating a FY24 acquisition/perimeter change. A standalone endpoint cross-check from ₹90.1991 crore to ₹1,061.3736 crore yields 127.45% CAGR and supports substantial growth beyond the acquired business, but is not a complete organic price/volume decomposition. CARE reports 750 MW capacity in December 2024 and 1,100 MW in December 2025; management reports FY26 utilization of 76% of 1.1 GW. Physical capacity evidence supports real scale, while independently reconciled shipments and realized ASP remain unavailable.

The FY26 press release labels ₹1,067.60 crore as revenue, although ₹3.33 crore is other income; canonical growth uses operations revenue. Management's rounded H2 total income of ₹725.22 crore and owner PAT of ₹42.33 crore indicate seasonality, not a basis to annualize one half-year. REV starts at the high-growth anchor of 9, then is capped at 8 for a short changing-business history and Medium confidence. No further growth bonus or automatic small-base penalty is applied.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The 23 May backlog update reports approximately ₹2,210 crore of ongoing orders. Management distinguishes a roughly ₹1,500 crore BESS tender from approximately ₹1,150 crore of EPC execution, with the remainder maintenance, and targets 60% of EPC in FY27 and 40% later. Neither the tender total nor the maintenance component is treated as immediate revenue or cash.

The model separately builds module revenue as capacity × utilization × rupees per watt, then adds legacy services and BESS. Base FY27 modules contribute ₹1,080 crore using 1,500 MW average capacity, 60% utilization and ₹12/W. Legacy services of ₹145 crore and BESS of ₹400 crore give total revenue of ₹1,625 crore, close to management guidance but below its approximately ₹690 crore FY27 BESS execution target. The 1.9 GW expansion remains an explicit scenario assumption until commissioned and qualified output is verified. Further bull-case capacity is uncommitted analyst upside.

Base cash investment includes ONWC and operating deposits at 30% of revenue, declining toward 28%, plus explicit capex. Legacy tax, debt service and cash reserves are separate. Modest machinery spend does not automatically fund inventory, advances and guarantees. The possible ₹750–800 crore battery/cell program is excluded from base economics and separately stressed as cash investment requiring hypothetical equity. CAP remains NS because attributable incremental project returns are missing. Strong nominal growth with persistent poor cash realization cannot earn an unqualified Growth Quality score: the cap would be 5, while the incomplete score remains NS.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter-group ownership of 73.45% at 30 September 2026 gives a large economic stake but concentrates control. Declared encumbrance is zero; this is not a blanket assurance about all off-balance-sheet exposures. Executives have industry experience and delivered observable manufacturing growth.

Specific contrary evidence matters. FY26 purchases from Sadashiv Projects were ₹122.7128 crore and sales ₹42.8245 crore. Three connected debit creditor balances total ₹23.4835 crore and require pricing, delivery, recoverability and balance-sheet mapping checks. They are not added again to supplier advances without proof of non-overlap. Related-party transactions are not presumed improper. The company CSR penalty of ₹1.0247548 crore was upheld following appeal dismissal on 13 November 2025; ₹0.04 crore of personal director penalties is excluded from company obligations. Reported current CSR compliance and settlement of a subsidiary's prior shortfall do not independently establish settlement of the historic penalty.

KC Parikh resigned on 4 June 2025 after a proposed audit-fee increase was rejected. Its annexure says missing information was not applicable and states no other material reason. This must not be represented as evidence of audit obstruction. The execution record is mixed: CARE supports 750 MW in December 2024 and 1,100 MW in December 2025; IPO deployment ran beyond FY25 and was reported fully used by June 2025; the September 2026 expansion and FY27 BESS targets remain unverified/future goals. IPO monitoring identified commingled cash-credit accounts and relied on CA/management certificates while reporting no object deviation. Proposed May warrants were not issued according to the September filing, so no proceeds or dilution are assumed received.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 owner PAT is ₹75.1829 crore versus group PAT of ₹75.1948 crore; group CFO of ₹20.9546 crore is compared with group PAT. Removing ₹3.33 crore of other income gives operating EBIT of ₹100.7406 crore and EBITDA of ₹110.2542 crore, a 10.36% margin. The press-release EBITDA includes other income.

The cash-flow bridge starts with PBT of ₹98.2589 crore, adds depreciation of ₹9.5136 crore and financing costs of ₹5.8116 crore, and removes interest income of ₹0.7356 crore. Inventory, loans/advances, receivables and other current assets use ₹57.4074, ₹71.8518, ₹6.1868 and ₹2.2653 crore respectively. Payables and other current liabilities provide ₹33.4605 and ₹22.7908 crore; long liabilities use ₹0.0841 crore and provisions provide ₹0.2642 crore. After ₹10.6141 crore tax paid, CFO is ₹20.9546 crore with ₹0.0001 crore rounding. Thus weak CFO reflects operating investment rather than capex. Cash capex of ₹15.4269 crore gives reported FCF of ₹5.5277 crore; subtracting ₹19.0996 crore of noncurrent-asset outflows and financing costs leaves approximately minus ₹19.38 crore. FY24–FY26 reported FCF totals minus ₹38.95 crore.

The FY24 prospectus CFO of ₹0.1708 crore conflicts with the later comparative of ₹24.8458 crore; investing classifications explain part, not a complete bridge. FY26 printed cash-flow closing cash of ₹27.7899 crore conflicts with components of ₹25.2915 crore and the ₹25.2916 crore rollforward. Both were visually checked; no missing-cash allegation is made. Bank FDs and security deposits need a pledge/release map, not an overpledge accusation. CARO flags absent inventory-movement tracking across sites while calling physical verification appropriate. Implausibly printed bank-limit units, older lender-return differences and incomplete MSME identification reinforce the G2 hold. The 29.50% average-capital post-tax proxy is not attributable incremental ROIC; CAP remains NS.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹221.20, market capitalization of ₹548.59812 crore implies 7.30× FY26 owner PAT, or 7.55× the cautious normalized PAT proxy of ₹72.6854 crore. Using March current-account/cash-on-hand balances of ₹18.1311 crore, excluding all bank FDs and operating deposits, gives a historical EV cross-check of ₹584.59672 crore including NCI, or 5.30× operating EBITDA. This is not a verified current net-debt estimate.

Bear/base/bull terminal EV/EBITDA multiples are 5×/7×/9×. Annual models include margins, ONWC, capex, debt service and minimum cash of 2% of revenue. Operating property is not added again. Every ordinary return and entry price is null because current funding is unverified. Each non-rescue path also has an in-horizon gap, so conditional returns are null. The base peak gap is ₹195.50 crore under explicit working-capital assumptions, not proof that actual financing is impossible.

The separate hypothetical rescue at a 20% issue discount and 2% issue cost requires ₹199.49 crore gross, dilutes existing ownership by 31.25%, and mathematically produces a 20.66% five-year annual return. Rescue bear and bull returns are minus 9.43% and 42.71%. They are not R scores or forecasts. Sensitivities cover revenue/multiple, collection delay/margin, opening cash, claims, issue costs, discounts, hurdle rates and execution costs. The reverse 15% hurdle requires approximately ₹1,635.82 crore of terminal revenue at 7× EBITDA and 10% margin, assuming no dilution or excess cash and the modeled claims. This says nothing about fundability. A 9× normalized-PAT cross-check does not add cash again. Terminal operating metrics interpolate FY31/FY32 to 19 October 2031; only the FY32 cash fraction through that date is funded, with later gaps reported separately.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not simply a lower quoted P/E. A large fixed-price BESS or module contract can combine an imported-input/FX shock, delayed inspection and slow customer collection. Inventory and advances stay funded while margins fall. Guarantee margins, taxes and debt service consume cash, creating refinancing or equity needs precisely when investor confidence is weakest. A 20% issue discount is not a guaranteed financing floor; deeper-discount and fee sensitivities show the ownership consequences.

Counterevidence includes the actual profitable scale-up, modest historical leverage and CARE's adequate-liquidity assessment. Automatic insolvency claims would therefore be inappropriate. Yet growth that repeatedly fails to convert profit into cash can permanently impair minority value even when orders are eventually completed. The bear path assumes lower utilization/ASP, 6.5–7% EBITDA margins, 35–36% ONWC, a disputed-tax loss and an external guarantee call. It needs ₹201.72 crore before hypothetical rescue. A terminal number derived from an unfunded path is not an investor return, and the model gap alone does not prove actual funding failure.

Recoverable value depends on saleable inventory, collectible government/customer balances and productive assets, not repeated additions of deposits or promoter-owned property. The single thesis-break variable is reliable cash conversion after project deposits and all claims. Permanent-impairment risk is assessed High, not a proven severe fraud/default condition. Demonstrated misuse, material connected-advance impairment or a loss-making BESS contract would be more damaging than ordinary share-price volatility.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold price growth over five years requires 37.97% annual appreciation; tenfold requires 58.49%. At the present share count and ₹221.20 reference price, 5× and 10× terminal equity values are ₹2,742.99 crore and ₹5,485.98 crore before dilution. At 7× EV/EBITDA and a 10% margin, even ignoring net claims, those values imply approximately ₹3,918.56 crore and ₹7,837.12 crore of annual revenue. Actual claims would raise the requirement unless offset by truly excess cash.

Current capacity and the existing BESS order do not independently establish sustained growth to either scale. Financing with new shares raises the total business value needed for the same return per original share; the base hypothetical rescue already dilutes ownership by 31.25%. Integrated cell or battery investment could expand the opportunity but adds the indicated ₹750–800 crore capital burden and execution/obsolescence risk, not free optionality. The bull rescue can mathematically exceed 5× only under uncommitted scale, margin and funding assumptions. The appropriate feasibility classification is Speculative/unsupported as an investment forecast. No probability of achieving 5× or 10× is assigned.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Eight company-specific checks are recommended, not scheduled automatically:
1. Reconcile FY27 half-year/full-year operations revenue to ₹1,500–1,700 crore guidance, separating modules, BESS EPC and maintenance. Revenue growth accompanied by unbilled assets rather than collections warrants investigation.
2. Track CFO less project/noncurrent deposit outflows against the FY24–FY26 baseline of minus 26.74% of PAT. Require sustained improvement rather than a one-time supplier stretch.
3. Follow inventory of ₹172.66 crore and supplier advances of ₹47.00 crore through inspection, dispatch and collection. Material unrecoverable balances would break the thesis.
4. Obtain certified available cash, FD restrictions, operating deposits, drawn limits, unused committed cash lines and guarantee margins. Printed facility-unit errors cannot establish funding capacity.
5. Track the approximately ₹1,150 crore BESS EPC schedule, excluding maintenance, and examine customer advances, liquidated damages, input/FX protection and loss provisions.
6. Resolve the FY24 cash-flow comparative, FY26 closing-cash line, site inventory records and MSME classification. Repeated material unexplained differences keep G2 on hold.
7. Substantiate connected purchases of ₹122.71 crore and debit creditor balances of ₹23.48 crore through pricing, delivery, recovery and once-only classification; monitor the ₹4.75 crore external guarantee.
8. Verify CSR/tax outcomes, warrant allotment versus proposal, physical 1.9 GW commissioning and any new cell/BESS capex commitment with its own financing and return case.

Reassess after material filings and each half-year report. Before implementation, refresh quote, lot, 20/60-session activity, live bid/ask depth and surveillance restrictions. Thresholds trigger research, not automatic trades.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
The classification is Hold — unresolved, with high research priority but no favorable investment conclusion until critical evidence clears. This is not Avoid — governance: GOV 4 and G1 Conditional do not establish severe abuse. It is not an evidenced funding-failure verdict: G3 is Hold rather than Fail. NS aggregates belong in a pending-evidence category, not at the bottom of a fabricated numeric ranking.

A change requires a current bank-sanction/drawing-power and cash/deposit bridge, complete accounting reconciliations, attributable project/cohort capital returns and demonstrated realization of inventory/advances. Weak cash conversion and a contestable moat remain concerns even if disclosure errors prove clerical. A lower price improves some valuation arithmetic but cannot manufacture verified funding or reliable claims. For an existing holder, the relevant issue is cash, governance execution and dilution rather than the purchase price. Holdings, taxes and risk tolerance were not supplied, so no personalized position or forced-sale instruction is inferred.

The actual 300-share SME lot costs ₹66,360 at the reference close. Seven lots are 2,100 shares costing ₹464,520; eight are 2,400 shares costing ₹530,880, straddling the ₹5 lakh illustration. The 60-session conservative turnover implies 1.84 theoretical exit days at 5% participation, while the weaker 20-session measure implies 2.74 days. Whole-lot capacity and unobserved depth warrant caution. No orders, external communications or scheduled monitoring are performed by this dossier.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The research uses annual reports, the prospectus, official exchange archives, credit rationales, IPO monitoring, board decisions, shareholding disclosures and the management transcript. Verified reported facts (V), calculations (C), management statements (M) and analyst assumptions (A) are distinguished. Exchange price and security-master data are dated 19 October 2026; the latest verified financial balance sheet is 31 March 2026, not an inferred October statement.

The register preserves URLs, document dates, locators and SHA-256 hashes. Private backup archives exclude raw issuer PDFs, OCR, images and personal identifiers. Safe extracts reproduce arithmetic, not independent rereading of omitted original documents. Two CRISIL peer pages were inspected through the primary web reader, but direct shell retrieval returned HTTP 406; their hashes identify analyst fact extracts, explicitly not original page bytes. No later event is used to improve the cutoff conclusion.

Open issues include corrected facility units and current unused lines; restrictions and release dates for deposits; a full comparative cash-flow bridge; inventory and MSME controls; connected-advance mapping; government/statutory/tax overlap; IPO expense timing; and incremental returns on new projects. Missing evidence is not treated as zero. The model states its dated opening assumptions, separate hypothetical rescue, minimum operating cash and partial terminal-year funding. All returns are nominal INR before investor taxes; sensitivities are not confidence statistics. Reproduction verifies computation and bytes, not issuer truth, forecast validity or an investment outcome.
